questions.prompt: When MS-DOS runs a program, it creates a new process for it.
When MS-DOS loads a program, what does the program overwrite?
options: All of memory except the kernel, including most of the command interpreter

questions.prompt: What happens when a program exits in MS-DOS?
In FreeBSD, which system call does the shell use to create a new process? (one word)
Which system call loads a program into the newly created process? (one word)
After fork() and exec(), what can the FreeBSD shell do?
options: Only wait; it can't do anything else
Wait for the process to terminate, or continue taking user commands
Nothing; the shell has been overwritten

questions.prompt: A FreeBSD process exits with code 0. What does that mean?
In FreeBSD, the command interpreter stays in memory while other processes run.
